\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بررسی} \fa{کردن} (barrasi kardan)}{بررسی کردن (barrasi kardan)}]{\fa{بررسی} \fa{کردن} (barrasi kardan) — to check, to examine}

\label{lesson:FA-C259-barrasi-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to agree, then the Persian for to imagine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بررسی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{بررسی} \fa{کردن}} — \emph{barrasi kardan} — \textquotedblleft{}to check, to examine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{barrasi kardan} pairs \emph{barrasi}, \textquotedblleft{}examination\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{kardan}. \emph{barrasi} is \emph{bar}, \textquotedblleft{}on\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{rasi}, \textquotedblleft{}reaching\textquotedblright{} (from \emph{residan}): going over a thing. All are native Persian. \emph{kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb, from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{چانه} \fa{زدن} (châne zadan)}{چانه زدن (châne zadan)}]{\fa{چانه} \fa{زدن} (châne zadan) — to haggle, to bargain}

\textbf{\fa{چانه} \fa{زدن}} — \emph{châne zadan} — \textquotedblleft{}to haggle, to bargain\textquotedblright{}.

\emph{châne zadan} is \textquotedblleft{}to strike the chin\textquotedblright{}, to haggle: \emph{châne}, \textquotedblleft{}chin\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{zadan}. Both are native Persian. \emph{zadan}, \textquotedblleft{}to strike\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{zadan}.
